Let \(q=3^r\). I claim
\[
\boxed{
M_r=
\begin{cases}
\dfrac{5q^3+q^2+7q+3}{8},& r\ \text{odd},\\[6pt]
\dfrac{(q-1)(7q^2+4q-3)}{12},& r\ \text{even},
\end{cases}
\qquad q=3^r.}
\]

**Solution**

Since \(L\cap F=0\), every such \(L\) is the graph of a linear map \(S:E\to F\). The graph is Lagrangian exactly when \(S=(s_{ij})\) is symmetric. The condition \(\jmath(L)=L\) forces \(S\) to commute with the sign decomposition of \(\jmath\), so all mixed parity entries vanish:
\[
s_{12}=s_{14}=s_{23}=s_{34}=0.
\]
Thus, with
\[
a=s_{33},\quad b=s_{24},\quad c=s_{22},\quad d=s_{13},
\]
and using \(s_{11}=s_{44}=1\), we have
\[
S_{+}=\begin{pmatrix}1&d\\ d&a\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
S_{-}=\begin{pmatrix}c&b\\ b&1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Also
\[
A=a+2b,\qquad B=c+2d.
\]

The determinant condition becomes
\[
a-d^2+c-b^2=A+B-1-\Delta.
\]
Since \(A=a+2b\) and \(B=c+2d\), this simplifies in characteristic \(3\) to
\[
\Delta=b^2+d^2+2b+2d-1=(b+1)^2+(d+1)^2.
\]
For fixed \(A,B\), the number of possible \((b,d)\) is therefore the number of solutions to
\[
u^2+v^2=\Delta,
\]
where
\[
\Delta=A^2B^2-A^3-B^3.
\]

Now compute the condition \(\rho_t(L)\cap F=0\). For
\[
v_t=e_1+te_2+t^2e_3+t^3e_4,
\]
one has
\[
v_t^T S v_t
=
1+Bt^2+At^4+t^6.
\]
The rotation \(\rho_t\) sends some nonzero vector of \(L\) into \(F\) exactly when this scalar is \(0\). Hence we need
\[
t^6+At^4+Bt^2+1\neq 0
\qquad\text{for all }t\in\mathbb F_q.
\]
Writing \(z=t^2\), this says that the cubic
\[
g_{A,B}(z)=z^3+Az^2+Bz+1
\]
has no root among the nonzero squares of \(\mathbb F_q\).

Let \(H=(\mathbb F_q^\times)^2\), so \(|H|=n=(q-1)/2\). We count pairs \((A,B)\) for which \(g_{A,B}\) has no root in \(H\).

For each \(\alpha\in H\), the condition \(g_{A,B}(\alpha)=0\) is one affine line in the \((A,B)\)-plane, hence has \(q\) points. For two distinct \(\alpha,\beta\in H\), there is exactly one cubic with those two roots and constant term \(1\). For three distinct roots in \(H\), their product must be \(-1\).

If \(r\) is odd, then \(-1\notin H\), so no three elements of \(H\) can have product \(-1\). Hence
\[
T=q^2-nq+\binom n2
=\frac{5q^2+3}{8}.
\]

If \(r\) is even, then \(-1\in H\). The number of unordered triples of distinct elements of \(H\) with product \(-1\) is
\[
\frac{n^2-3n+2}{6},
\]
because among ordered triples \(xyz=-1\), there are \(n^2\) total, and \(3n-2\) with at least two equal. Thus
\[
T=q^2-nq+\binom n2-\frac{n^2-3n+2}{6}
=\frac{7q^2+4q-3}{12}.
\]

It remains to weight these admissible \((A,B)\) by the number of \((u,v)\) satisfying \(u^2+v^2=\Delta\). The expression
\[
\Delta=A^2B^2-A^3-B^3
\]
is the discriminant of \(g_{A,B}\) in characteristic \(3\).

If \(r\) is odd, then \(-1\) is nonsquare. Hence
\[
\#\{(u,v):u^2+v^2=m\}
=
\begin{cases}
1,&m=0,\\
q+1,&m\neq 0.
\end{cases}
\]
The admissible cubics with \(\Delta=0\) have a repeated root \(\lambda\in\mathbb F_q^\times\). Their roots are \(\lambda,\lambda,-\lambda^{-2}\). Since \(-1\) is nonsquare, the third root is never square; admissibility only requires \(\lambda\notin H\). Thus there are
\[
D_0=\frac{q-1}{2}
\]
admissible pairs with \(\Delta=0\). Therefore
\[
M_r=D_0+(T-D_0)(q+1)
=
\frac{5q^3+q^2+7q+3}{8}.
\]

If \(r\) is even, then \(-1\) is square. Hence
\[
\#\{(u,v):u^2+v^2=m\}
=
\begin{cases}
2q-1,&m=0,\\
q-1,&m\neq 0.
\end{cases}
\]
But for every singular cubic, the third root \(-\lambda^{-2}\) is a square, so no singular admissible pair exists. Thus \(D_0=0\), and
\[
M_r=T(q-1)
=
\frac{(q-1)(7q^2+4q-3)}{12}.
\]

Therefore
\[
\boxed{
M_r=
\begin{cases}
\dfrac{5\cdot 3^{3r}+3^{2r}+7\cdot 3^r+3}{8},& r\ \mathrm{odd},\\[6pt]
\dfrac{(3^r-1)(7\cdot 3^{2r}+4\cdot 3^r-3)}{12},& r\ \mathrm{even}.
\end{cases}}
\]
